subject: Invariance Modelling with more than two groups

messages.author: f57c96af63c64056
messages.subject: Invariance Modelling with more than two groups
parts:
Hi,

I have a scale i wish to test across multiple groups. I have three groups in total and i want to see if the scale is valid for all three samples.
Looking at the literature, i only really see research that has used two samples for example here is a wonderful tutorial http://pareonline.net/pdf/v19n7.pdf

Is it possible in Lavaan to check for more than three groups. How does lavaan account for multiple comparisons if at all
Below is an example which should demonstrate the concept albeit with negative variances being produced

library('lavaan')
library('semTools')
data("HolzingerSwineford1939")

# Create a fictitious school
mydf <- HolzingerSwineford1939 %>%
  mutate(school = ifelse (id <= 100, 'c_colm', school),
         school = ifelse (school == 1, 'school_a',
                          ifelse(school == 2, 'school_b', school)))

# Beef up the number of samples so the CFA will run
myindex <- sample(1:301, 5000, replace = TRUE)
mydf_sample <- mydf[myindex,]

model <- '
visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'
mod_iv <- measurementInvariance(model, data = mydf_sample, group = 'school', strict = TRUE, estimator = 'MLR')

If anyone could point me in the right direction I would appreciate it very much

Thank you for your time

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Invariance Modelling with more than two groups
parts: Is it possible in Lavaan to check for more than three groups. How does lavaan account for multiple comparisons if at all

The same methods apply to an arbitrary number of groups.  The tests are omnibus, so when you constrain loadings, intercepts, etc. across groups, you do so across all groups, and the change in model fit tells you whether that set of constraints is tenable.  If not, you could perform pairwise follow-up tests constraining parameters across pairs of groups at a time, but I'm not sure that is advisable (haven't seen any literature demonstrating its utility).  You could ask on SEMNET, since this isn't a lavaan issue but a general SEM issue:

http://www2.gsu.edu/~mkteer/semnet.html
